newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares fall sharply, punters book profits.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares fall sharply, punters book profits.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange (DSE) reversed a fierce two-day buying spree to close sharply lower on profit taking by investors and speculators, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 18.05 points, or 2.40 percent, lower at 733.70.
"Brisk profit-taking by speculators at the prevailing higher prices was expected. ...This was probably a technical correction," said Suresh Aggarwal of brokers Jai Mata Securities.
Share prices had surged upwards in the last two trading sessions on a fresh central bank monetary policy which sought easing of liquidity for industry.
ACC lost 88 rupees to close at 1,560 on heavy selling by both speculators and foreign institutional investors, brokers said.
Larsen and Toubro was down 13.75 rupees to 225 on institutional sellling.
State Bank of India shed 18 rupees to 223.50, while TELCO lost 18.50 rupees at 422.50 on brisk selling by speculators, brokers said.
TISCO fell 7.60 rupees to 184 and ITC was down 12.25 rupees to 310 on selling by mutual funds, they said.
Bajaj Auto was down 10 rupees to 975.
